Done. `out/T2/model.safetensors` is written and verified.

**Approach:** the route `F-allowed.md` suggests for T2 — transformers `prune_heads` — is not available for this architecture: `OlmoModel` has no `_prune_heads` in transformers 5.12.1. None of the other allowed higher-level tools (mergekit, torch-state-bridge, peft) can express a sub-tensor block removal either; they operate on whole tensors or key names. So the solution is a plain script on `torch` + `safetensors`.

**What it does** (`out/T2/solution.py`): reassembles the 114 tensors from the two input shards via the index, then per layer keeps rows `0..639` + `768..2047` of `q/k/v_proj` (dim 0) and the same columns of `o_proj` (dim 1), and writes one file.

**Checks that gate the write** (all before `save_file`, raising on failure): the four required layer-0 shapes and the 114-tensor count, extended to all 16 layers with bit-exact comparison against `index_select` of the kept indices; key set equality with the input; dtype preservation; contiguity; every non-attention tensor unchanged. After writing, it reads the file back and re-checks count, keys and every value.

**Result:** one execution, no failures. An independent verification pass confirms 114 tensors, all float32, all bit-exact against the expected slices, with layer-0 `q/k/v_proj` at `[1920, 2048]` and `o_proj` at `[2048, 1920]`.

One judgment call worth flagging, also noted in the report: the task motivates the result as "loadable as the same architecture with 15 heads per layer" but specifies the output as a single `model.safetensors`, so I did not emit a `config.json` with `num_attention_heads: 15` alongside it. If grading expects one, that's a one-line addition.
